translations.text: The account of John son of Zebedee, the apostle and evangelist.
The account of John son of Zebedee, who leaned against the breast of our Lord Jesus at supper and said, “My Lord, who will betray you?” This account was written
by Eusebius of Caesarea, concerning Saint John. He found it in a Greek book, and it was translated into Syriac, as he learned about his way of life and his birth,
and about his residence in the city of Ephesus. From [?] and about his residence in the city of Ephesus after our Lord’s ascension into heaven.
After our Lord’s ascension into heaven, when the days of Pentecost had been fulfilled and the Advocate had come to the upper room,
and all the apostles had been filled with the Holy Spirit and were speaking [?] days, each one of them desired,
being filled with the Holy Spirit, to go out, proclaim, and announce the truth of the Only Begotten, God the Word,
to bring the great message of faith to all the nations under heaven. When Simon Peter had finished speaking, they
all said to one another, “Now that our Lord Jesus has fulfilled everything necessary for our weak human race, we too ought
to carry out diligently everything he commanded us. As he was ascending from us into heaven and blessing us, he told us,
‘Go out, make disciples, and baptize in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Everyone who believes and is baptized will live.’ So we too, my brothers,
ought to toil and work throughout the whole world, travel through its regions, proclaim the good news, and teach all those who, in the worship of idols
and the libations offered to demons, have knelt before carved images and fallen down to worship the accursed demons, the children of the left. Let us take this labor upon ourselves,
and let us make light dawn within the understanding that the Evil One has blinded. Let the father of falsehood be crushed beneath the feet of us all.”
When these words had been spoken among the blessed assembly of apostles, they parted from one another bodily,
each of them filled with the Holy Spirit, who proceeded from the Father and came to them,
as the beloved Son had promised them. Each one of them went to the land and region entrusted to him by grace.
When this holy virgin, John son of Zebedee, set out, grace accompanied him through the Spirit
of holiness, to guide him to the land of the Ephesians, where the leadership and authority of [?] prevailed. When he departed and left Jerusalem,
he set his face toward Ephesus. On the third day after he had set out on his journey, he took a wooden cross
and placed it facing east. He knelt down and prayed, saying, “My Lord Jesus, now that your promise has been fulfilled, and we have all received from your fullness,
grant to the crown of your disciples that wherever, my Lord, they recall your birth from the Virgin, your life among human beings,
your suffering on the cross, your death and your entry into the tomb, your resurrection on the third day, and your ascension into heaven to your Father,
the weak human race may be strengthened—the race that the Evil One deceived in its childishness, taking them captive and leading them astray to serve idols,
sacrifice to demons, and worship unfeeling stones. Yes, my Lord, hear me and answer me.”
And may the demons and Satan’s legions wail wherever one of us proclaims your gospel. May the whole company of apostles be enriched by the sound of your praise,
which thunders everywhere. May the demons tremble at the voices thundering within your church. And remember your church, which you purchased with your precious blood,
which your Father gave you, so that through it all creation might receive forgiveness. You, my Lord, are light from light. And because it pleased you, in your Father’s love,
you walked on earth and humbled your greatness to raise us from the depths to which the murderer had brought us down through his envy. And you said—and we heard with our bodily ears—
‘I and my Father are one,’ and ‘Whoever has seen me has seen God [?].’ With this confidence, my Lord, I in my youth implore you to hear my prayer.
For I too am confident that I have received the Holy Spirit along with my companions. And behold, I have received from the Spirit and have been filled.
Whatever I ask your Father in your name, he gives me. Nothing is too difficult for anyone who believes in you, and whatever they ask, they receive.
Yes, my Lord, grant that I may make a beginning in your gospel and advance in all truth. For I speak the truth: you are the Word who came forth from the Father from the beginning.
And you appeared to the world in a body descended from Adam, from the virgin Mary, who was preserved in her virginity. And there is no
time when the Father existed without you, or you without him. And you laid the earth’s foundations from the beginning.
Your compassion brought you down, and you entered through the virgin’s ear. You dwelt in her for nine months and came forth from her.
You lived in the world in lowliness and insignificance. You chose us out of the world so that the world might live through our preaching. But now, my Lord,
I am going to this region to which your heavenly grace has directed me. May they turn, become disciples, and be baptized in your name and in the name of the Father who sent you.
May they receive your Holy Spirit, who came forth from your Father and now dwells in us. May the carved images of error be overthrown.
Build temples for yourself in the city of priests, for your praise, and in place of the shrines for burnt offerings and libations to demons, altars for your hosts.
And may those who take the road and paths through our guidance turn to you and offer you praise at all times. Amen.” When Saint John had finished his prayer,
our Lord Jesus spoke with him from heaven [?] and said to him, “I have given you my peace, and I have not left you an orphan. Look, I am with you
until the end of the world. Do not be afraid, son of Zebedee. Go and preach, and do not worry about what you will say or what you will speak.
When you have turned this city and this region away from error, another company of disciples, who labor in the gospel,
will also come and see everything I do through your hands. Go, and do not delay.” When he had finished speaking with him, John rose
and traveled confidently along the road, rejoicing in the joy of the Holy Spirit. He was dressed in Palestinian clothing
and walked barefoot. As he traveled, he proclaimed the good news about our Lord Jesus Christ in the cities and villages for forty-eight days.
Some said, “He is mad.” Others said, “No, let us leave him alone. This man comes from a distant region and does not know our mighty gods.
But when he comes in and learns, then he will love them and offer sacrifices to them.” Many people from Asia, however, listened to him warmly,
believed, and accepted his preaching. In three days he baptized about two hundred of them.
And he set them on the way of truth. Then Saint John went out and traveled on toward the city of
priesthood. His practice was to eat once, from one ninth hour to the next, when he had finished his prayer: bread and vegetables with a dish of lentils,
which he would buy for himself from town to town. He ate and [?] only water. He disciplined himself so that he would not mingle with pagans.
Now this great and chosen man, as we found in the writings recorded on sheets in the archives of the wicked Emperor Nero,
this Saint John had come and reached the city of Ephesus. He raised his eyes and looked,
and there was smoke rising from within the city of Ephesus, for it was a pagan festival.
They were sacrificing to demons. He stood there in amazement, saying, “What is this burning? Look, it is covering the sun,
so that it cannot shine on the inhabitants of the city!” Overcome with sorrow, he went on and reached the southern gate.
He raised his eyes and looked, and there was an image of deceitful Artemis standing above the gate, painted for them with pigments.
Gold had been applied to her lips, fine linen cloths hung before her face, and a lamp was burning before her.
When Saint John looked and saw her, he gazed at her and sighed. He wept over the city, then left and went from there to
another gate. There he saw the same thing. He went around and saw the same thing at all the gates. Finally he approached the eastern gate
and spoke to an old woman who was standing there worshiping her. He addressed her in the language of the region,
“Woman, I see that you are advanced in years. Whose image is this that you are worshiping?”
She said to him, “Do you not know, my son, what you are looking at? This is our Lady, and her image came down from heaven.
She feeds all flesh.” Now he who was young in body and exalted above the whole company of his brothers, the holy and virgin John,
[?] at her and said, “Be quiet, old woman, whose mind has grown stale through filthy sacrifices! Do not tell me about Satan’s daughter.”
She bent down, filled her hands with dust and pebbles, and threw it into his eyes. He left and went away from there.
He withdrew a short distance and knelt down. He prayed and pleaded, putting his face between his knees, from the sixth hour until the ninth.
He wept and sighed, saying, “Lord God, powerful and mighty, patient and abounding in kindness, you are the one who, in the beginning, showed
patience for a hundred years over the calls to repentance made by Noah’s household, but they did not repent until the flood came and washed away that whole generation.
You are the one who sent your beloved, only Son so that the world might live through him. He came and did good things like you, because he came forth from you.
You are the one who, when the people of Israel worshiped the calf, devised a pretext and said to Moses, ‘Leave me alone, so that I may wipe out this people,’
although he was not holding you back. For you wanted him to plead with you, because you greatly desired that human beings should live.
Likewise, your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, when the Jews seized him to kill him,
He prayed and said, “Forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” These things, O Exalted One, have been in you from eternity.
They are also found in your Son, for you are one. Turn back, my Lord, the hearts of these misguided people, for look, they are shouting and crying out before demons.
You came and killed the Evil One. Do not let him raise his head in the assembly of this city. Do not let the sound of the roaring of the demons’ deceit be heard.
You died once and brought us to life with you. Drive Satan away, for look, he has brought down and bowed before an idol
the one who was created in your likeness, before the legions of his demons. Let the desolate idols be despised—not only those here, but also
those in every region through which our preaching spreads. Yes, my Lord, you taught us to go about in the world humbly and as people held in contempt.
Hear the prayer of your servant John, and I will enter this city carrying the sign of your cross. Direct my path toward the right.
Where you rest, let a house be found for me to rent and lodge in, until, my Lord, this city becomes your disciple and acknowledges your name.
When he entered through the gate of Ephesus, he looked to the right and saw a building there that had been built for bathing the body.
He turned aside there, and there was a bathhouse keeper named Secundus. Saint John spoke with him and said to him in the language of the region,
“I am speaking to you, sir: would you be willing to have a stranger work with you?” Secundus the bathhouse keeper said to him, “How much would you want from me per day?”
Saint John said to him, “Give whatever you are willing to give.” He agreed to pay him a hundred small coins a day, accepted him, and brought him in to work with him at his trade, supplying
firewood to those who heated the bathhouse. He stayed with him for forty days, receiving his daily wages each day.
Secundus the bathhouse keeper spoke to the saint and said, “I would like to know what you do with your wages.
Look, in all these days you have bought yourself neither shoes nor even a rag. Tell me whether the money is still there.
Otherwise, save up your wages with me, and I will buy you whatever you need, since you are a stranger and have no family here.”
Saint John said to Secundus the bathhouse keeper, “I have a master, and he commanded me and my fellow disciples
that no one should acquire gold or silver or copper in his purse, or two tunics. I cannot disregard his command.
Otherwise, he will be angry with me.” Secundus said to him, “Who is this master of yours, and what is his name? You ought to tell me,
in case he comes and brings a charge against me. If he is a harsh man, he may hand me over and even inflict great losses on me. For it is a hateful thing
and disgraceful in the eyes of the law for anyone to take in a slave without his master’s consent.” Saint John answered Secundus the bathhouse keeper,
“Do not be afraid, freeborn Secundus. My master will not be angry with you, for he himself sent me and directed me to you.” Secundus said,
“Then why did you not tell me before today that you are a slave and have a master?” Saint John said to him, “My master is in heaven,
and he does whatever he wishes on earth, in the seas, and in all the depths. At his command everything visible and invisible came into being.
He formed all creatures and made the lights in the expanse of heaven. Then he fashioned Adam in his image.
And when Satan came in his envy, he counseled Eve, and she listened to his words and led Adam into sin. He transgressed his commandment, and they left Paradise.
They became exiles and worked the ground. They were fruitful and multiplied and filled the earth. Satan went about devising schemes.
He filled all humanity with love for idols, so that they would sacrifice to demons and worship the work of their own hands.
He made them forget the Maker and honor those who were not gods. But he,
the good Lord, was patient with them until Noah, his friend. He made him a herald for a hundred years while he built himself the ark,
so that they might see, repent, and turn away from their evil deeds. But when they despised our Creator, his anger rose.
He sent the waters of the flood and washed them all away. After the waters of the flood had ceased upon the earth, the world was established anew from Noah.
Generations were propagated again, and the world was inhabited at the Creator’s command. But human minds inclined toward practicing injustice and wickedness,
and turning away from the living God. Then the compassion of humanity’s Maker was revealed, and he took pity on the whole lowly condition of our weak race.
He sent prophets to proclaim his truth, but they were unwilling to listen to them. Some they struck, and some they stoned. But in this time, which is the last,
he sent his one beloved, only Son, whom he has had for as long as he himself has existed. He entered through the ear of a human woman,
and dwelt in her for nine months without departing from the one who sent him. The heights and the depths are filled with him,
and are governed by him according to his Father’s will. When nine months were completed, he came forth from the human woman—the Word who became flesh.
Her virginity was never impaired. He grew bodily among human beings and lived among human beings like
a human being—he, the Word, God—except for sin. He reached the full maturity of thirty years and chose apostles for himself.
They tested him while he was traveling in the wilderness. He made wine from water at Cana, at a wedding feast. And bread was lacking.
He fed four thousand men, besides women and children, from five barley loaves. They ate and had food left over.
They picked it up and carried as much as they could to their homes. Again, on another occasion, he fed thousands in the wilderness,
after healing their lame and their sick. He opened the eyes of the blind, and some of them are still alive today. He made the deaf hear and cleansed lepers.
He raised the daughter of Jairus, the synagogue leader, after she had died. Look, she and her father are still alive in the Decapolis. If you wish to go, you can learn from her.
And he raised the widow’s son in the city of Nain as they were going to bury him, and Lazarus after they had laid him in the tomb for four days.
There are, then, many things for you to hear, if you will lend me your ear, believe, and become his servant, Secundus. After
thirty-two years, however, when the thirty-third year had begun, the Jewish people hated him.
They hated his good deeds, just as they had rejected his Father and made themselves a calf at Horeb. They handed him over to Pilate the governor.
They flogged him, stripped off his clothes, mocked him, and spat in his face. They wove a crown of thorns and placed it on his head.
They crucified him on a tree and gave him vinegar and bitter substances to drink. They struck him in his side with a lance. Then he cried out in a loud voice on the cross.
When the proclamation of the prophets was fulfilled, the sun grew dark from the sixth hour until the ninth, and darkness fell over the whole earth on Friday.
The front of the temple gateway was torn apart, and the round stones and rocks that blocked the entrances of the [?] around Jerusalem split open.
The dead came out and entered the city, crying out aloud. They came and bowed down before him as he hung on the tree.
Many of them were standing there, and they took him down from the tree. A man full of truth, Joseph the council member, wrapped him in fine linen
and laid him in a tomb. On the third day he rose from the dead. We saw him, and he spoke with us. We ate bread with him, and we touched him, believed, and were certain
that he is the Word who became flesh and dwelt among us. He ascended to heaven and sat down at the right hand of his Father.
He gave us authority to give life and blessings to everyone who believes in his name. He said to us, “Go out, make disciples, and baptize them
in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Everyone who believes and is baptized will live.” And now I appeal to you, Secundus.
For I have tested you during these days and found that you are not a blasphemous man, but are full of goodness and love strangers.
Accept what I have told you, and do not consider me a liar. If you wish, come with me to the region of Galilee,
and I will show you some of the dead, the blind, the bent over, the paralyzed, and the lepers whom he cleansed, healed, and raised to life, who are still living.
For if you do not wish to come, yet believe, you are greater than I, who saw him and was with him, because you believe that he who did these things is God.
He will turn you back, wash you clean, and sanctify you from the filth of unclean sacrifices. Yes, my brother, put my mind at rest, and your dwelling will be blessed,
and you will be known before him in the new world.” Secundus the bathhouse keeper sat astonished,
marveling at what he heard from John. He began to say to him, “What you have told me is astonishing and gives rise to wonder.
For even if he is not God and did not descend from heaven, and it is impossible for him to be believed in and called God
because he came out of the womb without destroying virginity as he came out, it is a great offense unless one acknowledges that he who raised the dead is God.
He who made wine from water is the Creator. He has authority over our bodily frame, and for this reason he opened eyes, healed, and cleansed.
This one deserves to be called God, and not this utterly powerless one. For sixty years now I have been giving her votive offerings and libations,
yet she has not opened the eye of my blind son. But now, my son John, let this secret that we have discussed be kept,
and let it not be revealed until the time when its Lord wishes to reveal it, especially since you are a stranger.
Otherwise, word may get out that you have not worshiped Artemis, and they may burn you. Now I have accepted, believed, and affirmed everything you have said.
But agree to my request and take charge of this bathhouse. Keep watch over the hired workers, and you will have authority over
the income and all the expenditure.” But John said to him, “It is not right for me to eat when I am not working.”
Secundus said to him, “Your labor is harder than that of the man who does the work.” Then the holy man was persuaded by him and agreed to receive the bathhouse’s income.
He gave an account from one morning to the next. Secundus and his household were amazed
at how much the bathhouse’s income had increased during those days, which amounted to twenty-two days.
He would come down especially early, speak with the holy man, and ask him, “How can you make me your companion?”
John, however, had been saying, ever since he had opened his son’s eye, that he should be baptized. On the twenty-fifth day, at an hour of the day,
a governor’s son named Menelaus, whose father was named Tyrannus, came and pressed the holy man to have the bathhouse closed and prepared.
But this man did not reveal to the holy man that someone would enter the bathhouse with him. The holy man gave the order, and the bathhouse was prepared.
This Menelaus came to bathe and brought a prostitute into the bathhouse with him. He was with her in the bathhouse.
When he came out from his bath, John stood up and said to him, “Do not come here another time, because you have brought great disgrace
upon yourself, who were created in the image of God: you went in with a prostitute and did not refrain from looking at her nakedness, while she looked at yours.”
But Menelaus became furious with the holy man and struck him. The holy man John said to him, “If you come here, you will not leave here.”
Two days later, he sent two of his servants to prepare the bathhouse. When the bathhouse was ready, he came to bathe.
He brought with him the same prostitute as before. But the holy man John, through the working of God our Lord, had gone out to inspect the furnaces.
When he returned, he asked, “Why is the bathhouse door closed?” They told him, “Menelaus, the governor’s son, is inside.”
When the holy man heard that he was inside and that a prostitute was with him, he became distressed, sighed, and was troubled. He waited until both of them had come out.
He did not look at them until they had covered themselves with their clothes. Once they had dressed after their bath, he turned and looked at them.
He said to the young man, “I am speaking to you! May Jesus rebuke you—he whom the Jews crucified on the cross, who died and rose after three days,
who is God, who ascended to heaven, and who is at his Father’s right hand. You shall fall and die where you stand!”
Immediately the angel of the Lord struck him, and he died on the spot. He lay there, while the holy man John remained seated in his place.
Immediately the prostitute went out wailing loudly, with her hands on her head. When those around the bathhouse heard,
they hurried over and saw that the young man was dead and lying there, with the holy man sitting beside him. They looked at his face and recognized
that he was Menelaus, the governor’s son. Groaning and wailing quickly spread throughout that marketplace. It was mealtime,
and his father was reclining, waiting for him to come up and eat with him. They went in and told him, “Your son, your only son, is lying dead in the bathhouse!”
Tyrannus quickly rose, threw ashes on his head, and tore his clothes. He hurried to the bathhouse to his son,
with a large crowd accompanying him. He came in and saw his son lying dead, with the holy man John sitting beside him. They seized John.
They put ropes on his hands and feet and heavy collars around his neck. Now the father of that young man
was wailing loudly. He gave orders, and they stripped John to see what he had on him. When they lifted his tunic and the worn-out cloth
in which he was wrapped, they found a cross hanging around his neck. It was made of wood.
The governor, the father of that young man, ordered them to remove it. When they stretched out their hands to remove it, four tongues of fire appeared on it.
They burned the hands of those who approached it. The whole crowd shouted, “This man is a sorcerer! Let this man be kept under guard today
and questioned about how many companions he has.” The governor ordered that Saint John be dragged away until he entered the prison,
while his young son was being buried. But the saint was shouting that the young man was not dead. His father gave orders, and they picked him up and turned him over.
He put his breath against his breath. But he was like an unfeeling stone. The saint, however, [?] said that he had not struck him, so that they might see that he was already [?].
The saint said to them, “If I struck him, I will bring him to life.” As they were dragging Saint John away to prison,
Secundus the bathhouse attendant stood among the crowd, weeping bitterly in sorrow. Saint John asked the tyrant
to summon Secundus the bathhouse attendant for him. The governor gave orders, and they seized Secundus and brought him
to him. Secundus was weeping over John, for he thought that John was going to be killed.
But the young man’s father thought that he was weeping over the young man. The saint replied, while [?], and said to Secundus,
“Do not be afraid, Secundus, and do not be distressed. Today the Holy Spirit has willed to reveal the truth.”
There was a large, unruly crowd. Saint John persuaded the governor to order the crowd to be silent.
He gave the order, and the crowd became quiet. Saint John stood up and cried out in a loud voice, saying, “I say to you, young Menelaus,
in the name of Jesus Christ, God, whom the Jews crucified and killed in Jerusalem, who died and was buried and rose after three days,
and who is now above in heaven at his Father’s right hand: rise!” Immediately he sprang up and stood. The entire crowd of the city was amazed.
The young man fell on his face before Saint John. He saw the collars placed around his neck and the ropes binding his hands and feet.
The young man untied them and kissed the tips of Saint John’s feet. Then the young man came forward and stood in a high place.
He waved his hand and began speaking from the beginning about how he had come to the bathhouse and everything that had happened. He related
in a loud voice before the crowd how he had committed sexual immorality with a prostitute and how the saint had ordered him not to come.
They began shouting, “Who did something to you that made you die?” He said to them, “This is what he said to me: ‘May my Lord Jesus rebuke you, whom the Jews crucified in Jerusalem,
who died and was buried and rose after three days, and ascended to heaven and sat down at his Father’s right hand.’
Immediately an angel struck me, and I fell. He [?] and took my soul. He brought me near, and I saw glory and a terrifying vision.”
For no human being can recount it as I saw it. But I will tell a little out of much, if this man standing before you gives me permission.
Immediately the young man’s father fell on his face before John and said to him, “I beg you, my lord, allow the young man to speak.
And do not be angry with him.” The holy man signaled to the young man to speak. The young man answered and said, “I saw a chariot of cherubim,
and countless seraphim with wings. They covered their faces so that they would not look at the Creator, and they cried out, ‘Holy, holy,
holy is the Lord Almighty! Heaven and earth are filled with his praises.’ And I saw twelve men in one group,
and seventy-two in the other. I counted them. They were standing with their heads raised toward heaven.
A right hand stretched out from among the cherubim, looking like fire, and commanded them in a gentle, pleasant voice, ‘Go out, make disciples
and baptize in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Everyone who believes and is baptized will live.’ And I trembled.
In fear I approached that great group of seventy-two, and again I begged them to tell me who this was.
They answered and said to me, ‘This is the Son of God, whom the Jews crucified in Jerusalem. He created everything you have seen.
At his signal it hangs suspended and stands firm. He sustains all the structures above, and by his power all the creatures below remain in existence.
For he is the Father’s power and wisdom. The Father sent him to save all those who cling to him and take refuge in him.
He draws everyone who believes in him and brings them to his Father. He is the one who declared, while walking on earth,
“I am the living bread that came down from heaven, and everyone who eats of my body will live.”’ And as I considered his true appearance,
I looked at that group of twelve and saw there this man who now stands before you, wearing splendid white garments.
He stood at the head of that group of twelve, beside an old man. The eyes of those eleven were looking at him lovingly,
so that he might offer some petition on their behalf. His own eyes were raised upward, and he was weeping. That old man approached
and asked him, ‘My son, why are you weeping and pleading like this?’ Now, when I asked that group of seventy, I learned
that the old man’s name was Simon. Holy John obliged Simon and said to him, ‘I am weeping because of the error of the city of Ephesus.
For look, she and her children are bowed down, and she worships the demons who dwell in ruined images.’
And I saw a gentle voice signal to him with a finger, ‘Go. Everything you prayed for before me has come to pass.’ And as I trembled, I recognized
that he was the one I had risen against to kill [?] in the bathhouse, because he had restrained me from sexual immorality. And while I was marveling at the many revelations,
my soul heard his voice and returned, and I came to life. And here I stand before you. From now on, even at this moment, I beg him
to bring me near to the living goal and make me his disciple. And you who have seen this miracle, turn away from error.
Let us despise the idols and become his disciples. Let us save our souls and not destroy them with our own hands. And when he sanctifies us,
Then let us give thanks and worship him, believing in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and at all times and forever
and ever. Amen. A large crowd had come and gathered there. He came out of the bathhouse to them, while the young man’s father held on to the holy man.
The young man himself came along with his hands raised toward heaven. They came and reached the great marketplace in the middle of the city.
The whole city gathered. It was the ninth hour, and the whole city was in an uproar:
men, women, and children. When the priests saw the sign that had taken place, and the young man standing there acting as a herald of the good news,
they said, “This man is a relative of Artemis our lady.” But Saint John cried out, “I am a human being, subject to suffering.
My Lord Jesus chose me, the Son of God who came down from heaven, entered through the ear of the virgin [?], and dwelt in her womb for nine months.
He came out of her without harming her virginity and lived in the world as a human being, apart from sin, though he is God,
like his Father. The Jews seized him and crucified him on a wooden cross in Jerusalem. He died and was buried, rose after three days, and ascended to heaven
and sat down at his Father’s right hand.” When the prefect, the young man’s father, heard these things, he fell facedown before the holy man’s feet,
as did all these leaders of the city, from the ninth until the eleventh hour. Men and women were amazed at these things. Half
of the crowd cried out, “Truly this mystery is great! Jesus ought to be worshiped, for he is God.” Others said, “Artemis ought to be worshiped.”
Those who had been found worthy to believe, together with their daughters and sons, numbered about thirty-six thousand seven hundred and six people
that evening, when they were counted at dusk. Their number was given to the prefect. There was great commotion and uproar,
and the day was drawing toward sunset. John supported the prefect to help him stand, saying to him, “Rise, sweet tree [?],
which has yielded its first fruits, whose fragrance is sweet and whose perfume spreads through the good news. Rise, my brother, and command your officials to stand with you.
Rise, and let your head be lifted up and no longer bowed. Do not worship me, for I am a servant, made and created. Rather, worship and give thanks to him,
to the one who formed us and created him.” All the officials raised their heads while kneeling on their knees
and looked at the holy man. They saw his face shining like light, and bowed their faces to the ground in fear. For they thought
that at that moment their lives among human beings were coming to an end. In fear [?], they raised their voices and cried out, “Truly great is
this God who has newly been proclaimed in this city of ours! These things are manufactured objects, not gods.
We are servants of this God, and we will no longer turn away to bow our heads before carved images,
which have not helped us and do not help us. We ask you, who are his servant: bring us before him,
so that we may know his ways, and show us his paths. For a good servant knows that whoever loves his master does his will,
and his master, in turn, listens to him.” When the holy man heard these things, he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and stretched out his hands toward them.
He had them stand up and said to them, “Peace to you, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom that is reserved for those who love him.”
“Stand up, new congregation gathered today to hear the good news of Jesus, the Son of God. I ask you, my brothers,
let us greet one another with a holy kiss, because the time is short, and the sun is completing its course, which it was commanded to follow by the one whom I proclaim to you.
Moreover, there are people here who have not yet tasted bread or water.” But they were shouting loudly, “Sweet
are your words to [?] my palate, better than honey to the mouth. For we truly hunger and thirst,
and we receive nourishment from your gracious word.” But Saint John urged the governor to dismiss the crowd,
while he prayed in his heart with groaning, saying, “My Lord Jesus, grant harmony to our congregation, and let Satan be driven away,
so that he may not stir up disturbance or rebellion in this city and harm anyone.” The governor stood up and waved his hand for them to be quiet.
When they became quiet, he began to speak to them. He said, “My brothers, my children, and my dear friends, if it seems good to you,
let us part from one another for now. Tomorrow morning I want you to gather in the theater.
We will do everything that is pleasing to the Spirit, which we have heard from this man’s mouth. For this is what we ought to do:
throughout the night, let everyone in his own house offer prayer and supplication before our Lord, who is in heaven and brings us near to his Father,
and concerning our sins, which have turned our feet away from his path, whether he wishes to include us among the congregations of those who praise him. And if not,
he will deliver us from the fire reserved for those who worship carved idols.” When the record keeper finished this reading, the whole crowd shouted
loudly, “Peace to you, wise governor! Peace to you, wise ruler! Peace to you, the young goat who came in and became a lamb! Today you have shown your love for us.
Today you have truly become our ruler, and you have advised us to live and not die.” When they finished shouting, after the officials had quieted them,
the crowd was dismissed, and they began to leave joyfully. The priests of Artemis gathered, sounded horns, and lit lamps.
The doors of the temple of idols were opened, and all the people of Ephesus ran to the temple of idols, as was their custom. But the governor became angry,
and he and the officials wanted to send men to kill the priests because they had held an assembly without their permission. But Saint John
threw himself on his face and pleaded with them: “Let no one who keeps my word and loves our Lord Jesus go and harm them there,
because they too, through your prayers, will draw near to the mystery of our life and become our brothers.” Then they yielded to the holy man.
Some of the officials, whose names were Antoninus, Marcellus, Epiphanius, and Pratontus, gave orders, and their servants ran
and brought a hundred and fifty lamps of [?] to give light. They pleaded with the governor,
“We ought not to disperse for this whole night, lest the city be set on fire by the worshipers of carved idols.” And they were saying
that fire had fallen upon their houses because they had abandoned the worship of Artemis. They were blaming Artemis, although she could do nothing.
And especially that they should not become murderers. When the crowd heard these things, they lifted Saint John onto their shoulders and ran.
In their joy they did not know what they were shouting. Those in front ran ahead and opened the doors of the theater.
The prefect and his officials entered with a great procession. They hurried to prepare and arrange a place for him, as was customary. But the prefect himself said:
“It is no longer right for me to sit on the throne. Take it away from here.” The whole crowd entered the theater, and there was a great commotion.
The sun had been set for about two hours. The men who served as the prefect’s own advisers
persuaded him to send out a thousand men to patrol the city and keep watch until dawn, so that nothing bad would happen.
Saint John urged that no one should be killed. If they caught anyone, they were to tell him, “There are two vigils in the city. One
is being held for Satan in the temple of Artemis, and one is being held for our Lord Jesus in the theater.
Go wherever you wish to go.” When the crowd heard these things, they rejoiced and stretched out their hands toward heaven, saying:
“Glory to you, Maker of heaven and earth, of night and day!” Then the prefect waved his hand to them and ordered them to be quiet.
He said to them, “Let our gathering not become a disturbance and an uproar. Instead, let us be quiet and hear the word of life, and see how we may live.”
He gave an order, and they brought Saint John up to the high platform. The officials sat at his feet.
The prefect remained standing and did not want to sit down, saying, “I ask you to let me stand, so that if anyone is physically weak,
I can go over and rouse him so that he does not fall asleep.” Only with difficulty was he persuaded to sit down. When he sat down, there was a great silence.
When they were quiet, Saint John sprang to his feet. He waved his hand to them to be quiet and took out the cross that was [?] at his neck.
He looked at it, placed it against his eyes, and kissed it. Weeping, he stretched out his right hand and made the sign of the cross over the whole crowd with it. He placed it on the high platform,
which was east of them all, and set up lamps before it. They cried out loudly and said:
“Servant of Jesus, tell us who this is that you have made for us!” The saint waved to them, and they became quiet. He began to speak and said:
“Beloved children whom the good news has won, this is the cross of the Son of God, who exists eternally with his Father.
He is the one who made these heavens and these stars arranged in them. All his creatures depend on him.
I have made this cross a wall of protection for you, so that Satan may not come and gather his demons and bring sleepiness or discouragement upon you.”
They cried out, “For us this night is day, for only now has our life drawn near to us!” Then they quieted one another.
When they were quiet, all the people ran forward. As they ran, he waved [?]. With their backs toward the west, they fell on their faces before the cross toward the east.
They wept and said, “We worship you, Son of God, who were hung on the wood.” The prefect was lying prostrate before the cross.
He went over and stood at the front and said, “We worship you, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.” And they all answered, “Amen.”
They said to John, “By our Lord Jesus, tell us what the place of the Son of God is, so that we may know whether we can approach him,
and whether he will forgive us for all the sacrifices and drink offerings with which we have defiled ourselves.” Then the holy man stood on a high step
and began to speak with them, filled with the Holy Spirit. He told them about the ordering of created things,
and that the Son of God was with him, with the Father, from the beginning, and was not separated or distant from him, and that without him nothing came into being:
everything in heaven and on earth, everything visible and invisible. And, filled with the Holy Spirit,
he recounted before them passages from the Law and the Prophets, and how God had compassion on the human race he had formed,
which was held captive by error, and sent his only Son. He came and entered through the ear of the Virgin Mary and dwelt in her womb for nine months.
He took a body from her, while the heights and depths were filled with him, and there was no place where he was not.
While forming infants in wombs, he was with his Father. When nine months were completed, he came out of the womb of a human woman,
while she remained a virgin. Her virginity was not harmed and remains forever. He grew up like a human being,
the great one who became small because he himself willed it. When he was thirty years old, he came to the Jordan for baptism
and was baptized by John son of Zechariah, who was his servant. When this Jesus was baptized, with crowds surrounding him,
heaven split open, and his Father cried out over him and pointed him out with his finger: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am pleased. Listen to him.”
Immediately he came up from the water, and the crowds surrounded him. And that hidden one who had come into the world began
to perform openly the miracles that he had been doing in secret. For he had been invited
to a wedding feast, and the wine ran out, and the bridegroom had none. He commanded the attendants and servants to draw water and pour it into the large basins
that were there. When the servants had filled them with water, he made a gesture and looked at the water, and it was blessed and transformed
and became pleasant, delicious wine. They all drank and enjoyed it, and I drank some of it. And while he was teaching in the wilderness, as the day was drawing toward sunset,
after the sick had been healed, the lepers cleansed, the lame had walked, and the eyes of the blind had been opened, those who had been healed were hungry.
There was little time left, and there was no bread except three barley loaves.
He commanded the crowds to recline, and at his command they brought him these loaves. He looked up to heaven, blessed and broke them, and gave them to them.
They ate and had more than enough and were satisfied. Those who ate and were satisfied, and carried some away to their homes, numbered, apart from women and children,
four thousand. He allowed us to get into the boat and cross the sea, while he remained on land.
When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, the sea rose against us, and we were tossed about all night. In the fourth watch of the night,
this very Jesus whom I proclaim to you came toward us, walking on the sea. We were terrified, and when he saw
One of the disciples, my companions, said to him, “My Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.” Jesus said to him, “Come.” And he walked and came toward him.
Our Lord Jesus came and entered the boat, and there was a great calm. These crowds were amazed and said, “Who can this be,
who commands the winds and the sea, and they obey him?” When Jesus came to the country of the Gadarenes, they brought to him
all those who were suffering from various diseases, those possessed by demons, the paralyzed, those with epilepsy, and the lame. And he healed them all.
And now, my brothers, the healings and signs performed by this Jesus, who is the Son of God, cannot be numbered or counted.
For as long as he appeared bodily in this world, he performed these works—the very works he had also been performing eternally while hidden in the one who begot him.
But he appeared in flesh from the Virgin and openly performed these signs, so that through them he might put Satan, the father of falsehood, to shame and condemn him,
and show the whole human race that everyone who is drawn and comes to him, he brings near to the Father who sent him,
and he performs works like these. For he and his Father are one. And because the Father loved the world, he handed him over to the cross. He died for us and gave us life,
and we live with him. Everyone who believes in him remains in him. As for what you asked me when you said to me, “Will our wrongdoing be forgiven,
along with our sacrifices, our drink offerings, our filth, and our uncleanness? And may we draw near to him?”—I now tell you:
If you believe in Jesus and resolve in your minds that you will no longer take part in the drink offerings and filth of idols, and none of you turns aside,
and you do not worship things made by human hands, but believe in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
I will do what he told us and commanded us when he ascended to heaven to his Father.
I will call upon him, and he will wipe away your sins, forgive your offenses, and whiten your stains. I will anoint your knees with oil and soften them—
those knees that you bent and that the evil one, our enemy, strained when he bent them before his idols, which have been made into a dwelling place for his demons.
I will seal you with his cross, which is the sign of life, upon the head that he bowed down to the ground.
He rejoiced that it was bowed down, because it had been created in the likeness of its Creator. And I will place a seal upon your foreheads,
so that when he sees that you are under the protection of that Lord, he will flee and say, “These were my young goats, and they were mingled with mine, to become great he-goats
and gore all ranks with their horns. But now the Son of the Father, who stooped down and became, from the Virgin,
flesh, has taken them and whitened their color, which was the darkness in which I am held. He has made them new lambs, and look, they stand beside him.”
And this mouth of yours, which was fattened at the table of the gods of fortune—and look, the deceitful one boasted, thinking he had made you food for the serpent—I will open it
and place in it the living bread, which is the body of God and gives life to everyone who believes in him. And I will give you the blood of the Son of God to drink,
who was pierced on Golgotha with a lance—the blood of this Jesus whom I am now proclaiming to you—so that even when you die, he is hidden within you.
His body and his blood remain in your flesh, and he will raise you from the dead. You will rise in this body, free from decay, and you will not come into fire and torment.
Nor will you see the worm that does not die in this incorruptible body, nor will you come to fire and torment.
Nor will you see the worm [?] that does not die, because you have believed in the name of the Only Begotten, who is the Son of God.
And truly, he is the one who gives life to the world. After this, the entire crowd in the theater cried out, saying:
“We ask you, servant of the living God: do whatever you wish, and let us share in the living mystery, so that we may live and not die.”
That is, at once. Then the holy man instructed the governor to provide him with a place in one of the corners of the theater.
Stonemasons came and worked immediately, making something in the shape of a basin. He diverted the conduit that brought water into the theater toward the basin.
The water came, and the basin filled up. Its dimensions were twelve cubits in length and twelve cubits in width.
It was two and a half cubits deep. Then the holy man asked the governor to order that fine, fragrant oil be brought:
seventy measures. He gave the order, and it was brought, and a trough was filled with it. The holy man approached, knelt down, and looked up to heaven.
He cried out in the middle of the theater, “Holy are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit forever. Amen.” And the entire crowd answered, “Amen.”
Then John made the sign of the cross over the oil and said in a loud voice, “Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit forever. Amen.”
Again, for the third time, he said, “Holy are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Amen.” Immediately, fire blazed above the oil.
Yet the oil did not burn, for two angels were spreading their wings above the oil and crying out:
“Holy, holy, holy is the mighty Lord.” When the crowd saw these things, they were filled with great fear.
They fell on their faces and worshiped toward the east. When the oil had been consecrated, the holy man approached the water and made the sign of the cross over it.
He said, “In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit forever. Amen.” All the people cried out, “Amen.” Immediately, these two angels
came and [?] over the water. They were crying out, “Holy, holy, holy are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, from his place.”
And Saint John cried out after them, “Amen.” Then John addressed the entire crowd, saying, “Stand up by the power of God.”
They all stood up in fear, with their hands stretched out toward heaven, and cried out, saying, “Great is this mystery!
We believe in the Father, and in the Son, and in the Holy Spirit.” It was about the eighth hour of the night. Then the governor approached
and fell on his face before John and said to him, “What should we do?” Saint John said to him, “Take off your clothes.”
When he had undressed, the holy man approached, took oil in his hand, made a cross on his forehead, and anointed his entire body.
He brought him to the basin and said to him, “Go down, my brother, for you have become a new firstborn, entering at the head of the flock into the fold of the Lord of the sheep. Go down, my brother,
for the lambs are watching you, and they are running to go down, become white, and acquire beautiful new wool in place of what was torn out by the wolves,
the vile ones.” The governor said, “What should I say before I go down?” John said to him, “In accordance with what you have seen, affirmed, and believed.”
The crowd was silent, as though no one were there, to hear what the governor and John were saying. But the governor
stretched out his hands to heaven and cried out, weeping, “I believe in the Father and in the Son and in the Holy Spirit.”
He sprang down into the baptismal font. Then the holy man approached, placed his hand on the governor’s head, and baptized him once, crying out,
“In the name of the Father.” “In the name of the Son”—that was the second time. And the third: “In the name of the Holy Spirit.” When he came up out of the water,
he then clothed him in white garments, greeted him with peace, and said to him, “Peace to you, new bridegroom, who had grown old and worn out in sin.
And look, today you have become a child, and your name has been written in heaven.” Then the whole crowd became excited, and they hurried eagerly,
each trying to run down to the baptismal font. But all the officials were standing around the font,
and they waved their hands at the crowd to quiet them. But the whole crowd cried out sincerely, saying, “Our brothers and our fathers,
let us run and anoint ourselves with some of this holy oil, and bathe in this water and become white. Perhaps the water will [?], or the oil
run out.” Then the holy man cried out to them and said, “Be quiet, blessed flock, for your Father in heaven wishes to give you his kingdom,
because you have believed in his beloved Son.” They immediately became quiet. Then the holy man approached and said to the governor,
“Come, sit in the fine high seat. For today you deserve to be honored, because there is joy in heaven on your account.” They prepared a place for him, and he sat down.
Then he waved his hand at them to quiet them. When they were quiet, he began to speak to them: “Truly, today our lives have been brought near to us.
Now, if this holy man gives me permission, I will speak.” Then the whole crowd cried out to John, saying,
“In the name of Jesus, give him permission to speak.” John said to him, “Speak, my lord, whatever you wish.”
Then the governor said, “Listen, my brothers. While I was being baptized, I opened my eyes and saw that I was not going down,
but going up into heaven. And the second time, I looked and opened my eyes, and a right hand holding a pen
was writing. And the third time, I heard a voice saying, ‘The sinner, the sheep that was lost, has been found. Let him enter.’”
Then holy John immediately clasped his hands behind his back and threw himself face down before the cross, crying out,
“Glory to you, Maker of all creatures, who sent your beloved Son, and he walked upon the earth and gave us authority to go out and proclaim his good news in the world,
and bring those who have gone astray back to repentance.” Then he spoke to the officials, and they took off their clothes. He approached and anointed them
and baptized them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. When they had been baptized, he then baptized the whole crowd,
from the eighth hour until sunrise. A great many people gathered and came. When morning came, they ran and brought their children,
and the holy man continued baptizing them until the fifth hour. Those who received baptism numbered
thirty-nine thousand, two hundred and five people. Then the crowd [?] and nine thousand, two hundred and five people.
Then the whole crowd dispersed that day. The governor took the holy man to his home, and they were happy and rejoiced.
He stayed with him for three days. On the third day, the holy man begged them to let him go and live on one of the mountains.
The governor sent for all his nobles and gathered them together. They begged John to remain in the palace, but he would not be persuaded, for he said:
“I must travel throughout Asia and also through the region of Phrygia.” When he saw that they were distressed and weeping, he said to them, “If
the Holy Spirit had wished me to go, you would not have been distressed. But now I will stay and remain with you.
Let us go out, however, and walk around the whole city, so that I may see where I should live, for my fellow apostles are coming to me.”
These words pleased them. The governor rode in procession, and all his officials went before him.
As they were going around, the holy man said, “I beg you, my brothers, to show me the place of worship of these misguided people.”
The governor and his troops came to the temple of Artemis. They wanted to kill the priests and burn her temple with fire.
But John pleaded that no one should be killed, saying, “These people will come and turn to the knowledge of the truth.
Let us not destroy them with [?].” When the holy man came and saw them and the house of foolishness,
there was a high place there. He saw that place and said, “I want to live here.”
The governor and the officials ordered that a palace be built for him there. But he said, “No, by my Lord Jesus!
If you build anything, I will not live in it. I want nothing but a shelter.” Immediately they brought materials and made him a shelter situated above the temple of
the idols. He lived beneath it. While he stayed there for a long time, people flocked to him:
all those who believed in Jesus Christ our Lord. They were baptized, and he gave them communion in the body and blood of Jesus.
There was a shelter above the temple of Artemis. The holy man lived there and saw the impurity that took place there.
After three months and ten days, the priests gathered together. They went around and announced to the gathering of pagans,
“We must hold a festival for our goddess. Let everyone prepare whatever he can afford, along with bulls and sheep, and let us offer sacrifices
and see why our goddess is angry with us.” Then the pagans gathered, made preparations, held a festival, and offered unclean sacrifices.
While they were gathered, John stood above them in the shelter, watching everything that happened. As they knelt before her,
they said to the priests, “Ask her the reason, and find out from her on whose account she has held back her hands and become angry with us human beings.”
There was division in the city. Then Legion came, the sister of the one who had fallen into the sea with the pigs.
She spoke through the ruined images. The priests listened and heard buzzing sounds, like those of bees, coming from the mouth of the image.
They quieted the pagans, approached, and put their ears to the mouth of the image. The demons raised their voices and said:
For that hut will tear down this house. Do not fight with him. For, as that great one of ours said:
“He fought with this man's master, and this man's master defeated him. Take heed, then, and be afraid of him yourselves. We too are afraid,
lest his master come to this man's aid, become angry, and throw us into the abyss, and our master be deprived of two legions.”
But here we are, fighting so that we will not be defeated. If he defeats us, we are reckoned like his master, who defeated our master.
The priests were trembling, and they answered, “We beg you, our lords: who is this man's master?” The demons said:
“He is the Son of God, who came down from heaven. Our master did not notice when he came down, became a human being, and died on the cross.
Our master thought he was an ordinary man. But on the third day he rose from the tomb, and now he is in heaven, threatening us.”
When the priests heard these things, they were bewildered and astonished. The crowds said to them, “Why are you astonished?”
The priests answered, “Artemis said [?] that this hut will tear down this house. All her confidants are afraid
of this man. They were also urging us to be afraid of the one who lives in this hut, saying, ‘If he wishes and gives the command, he will cast us into the abyss.’”
Immediately the crowds began shouting, “We renounce this Artemis! She is of no use!
For if this man, who is a servant or disciple, has such mighty power, how much more does his teacher or master!” They struck their faces and said:
“Alas! What has happened to us? Our courses have ended in [?], and we have traded at a loss to our souls.” But the priests said:
“You know for yourselves. Do whatever seems right to you. But we worship the one who can give life and destroy,
and we honor him.” They hurried down from the upper room [?] and ran up to the holy man. They threw themselves facedown before him.
The entire crowd threw ropes around the statue of Artemis, pulled it down, and dragged it along, while groups ahead of her and behind her shouted:
“Destroyer of our lives, get up and save yourself! You did not come down from heaven. Craftsmen made you in a furnace!”
Saint John saw the priests lying facedown. He did not speak to them, nor did they speak to him.
He knelt among them and turned them to face east. He prayed and pleaded. While the crowd was shouting and dragging
the statue of Artemis, the congregation—those who had previously received baptism inside the theater—
were acclaiming them with scarves and garments, saying, “Welcome, our brothers and our children!
Let us all be one soul. Welcome, congregation that was angry with its Lord! Today it has returned and joined our number.
Welcome, flock that Satan had taken captive! Its Lord has brought it back so that vicious wolves will not tear it apart.”
When the governor heard the uproar and the loud shouting throughout the city, he trembled. He got up and came from his palace,
and went up to Saint John. He found him kneeling. The governor raised his hand for them to stop shouting, and gave an order.
Strong men stood up to restrain the crowd so that it would not go up to John. Then the governor said to Saint John:
“Stand up, my lord, and seal this new assembly. Otherwise, their lives will be exhausted [?] from shouting.
For I see old men whose clothes are soaked with tears and sweat.” Then the saint lifted his head from prayer
and said to the governor, “I was pleading for them before our Lord Jesus Christ, that he might enter and present [?] them before his Father
and intercede for them. For he is the gate, and through him a person enters and finds pasture. And without him, to the Father no one
draws near. He himself gave the law from Mount Sinai.” Then the saint stood up and looked down at them from above, and he sealed them with the sign of the cross.
They all fell on their faces before him, crying out in sorrow and anguish, “We have sinned, acted foolishly, and done evil,
and we did not know until today. Have mercy on us, my Lord, Lord of heaven and earth. From now on we renounce all idols.”
Then the saint called down to them from above, “Rise by the power of our God! Rise in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, his beloved Son!”
Immediately they rose. They lifted their hands toward heaven and cried out, “Glory to you, God, maker of heaven and earth!
Appear to us, our Lord, so that we may know that you are the true God and that this young man was sent by you to the city of Ephesus.”
A cloud was overshadowing the city, and immediately there was a gentle peal of thunder. The entire crowd
fell on their faces in fear and said, “We acknowledge you, hidden God who cannot be seen. Now you have revealed yourself to us according to your will [?].
We profess our faith in you, and there is no other God besides you.” Then Saint John himself spoke with them and was explaining
to them from the Law and the Prophets. He taught them about our Lord Jesus, confirming and showing them concerning our Lord Jesus
that he is the Son of God. Once they had accepted the faith, they pleaded to receive the seal of baptism,
crying out and praising God. The governor himself appealed to the saint, saying, “If you wish, my lord,
let us send heralds out into the city to proclaim that everyone who believes in the Son of God should come, wash, and be cleansed of impurity.
Let us go to the place where the baptismal pool is, and give everyone who comes the seal, so that he may live and not perish.”
Saint John said to the governor, “You have spoken well, my lord. We will do as you command.” Immediately they both stood up.
The governor raised his hand for them to be quiet. When they were quiet, he said to them, “We are speaking to you, new children whom the gospel of God has gained.
Today, as we are all gathered together, go without disorder to the theater, for there you will receive the seal of life.”
As they gathered, they formed groups, crying out and saying to the governor, “How should we chant and sing?”
The governor said to them, “Say and sing this until you enter: ‘Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.
Lord, have mercy on us.’” The sound of their shouting carried more than five miles beyond the city. They came and entered the theater.
Then the governor and John came and entered the theater. Then the holy man spoke up and waved his hand for the crowd to be quiet.
When they were quiet, the holy man stood on the steps and said, “Stand up for prayer.” They turned toward the east and fell on their faces.
They were saying, “Lord, have mercy on us.” Then the priests came in at the back, while they and all the people were lying on their faces.
They walked barefoot, wrapped in sackcloth, with dust scattered on their heads and their faces covered with soot. They were wailing and crying out:
“God who sits in heaven, have mercy on us! We have sinned before you, and we have led countless souls into sin.
It is not difficult for you to forgive us, if you wish.” When they had said this, John rose from his prayer and said, “Stand up by the power of God.”
When they stood up, he concluded the prayer, and they all answered, “Amen.” Then he turned and looked at the seven priests,
who were standing in a disgraceful state, their heads bowed toward the east and their hands raised toward heaven.
Endless tears flowed from their eyes and ran down their soot-blackened cheeks. When the holy man saw this,
he was grieved and wept, and the governor wept with him. The whole crowd was weeping. Then the holy man knelt down
and prayed, saying, “Merciful God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who sent him, you, my Lord, said:
‘If the wicked person turns away from his wickedness and does what is right before me, he will live by the righteousness he has practiced.’
I ask you, my Lord: have mercy on what your hands have formed, and do not turn away from it. Let us welcome these who were lost
like sheep without a shepherd, so that they may praise your great and awesome name, and your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.
For to you, to him, and to your Holy Spirit belong praise and honor forever. Amen.” The whole assembly answered, “Amen.” Then he stood up and called them, but they
could not speak because of their weeping and sobbing. He approached them, holding the governor by the hand.
He spoke with them, but they did not speak. Then the holy man traced a cross on the forehead of each one of them.
Then a cry arose from the whole crowd, and the tears of holy John were pouring down. He said to them,
“Take courage! There is no cause for despair. Hope has been given to humanity through the birth of the Son of God from the virgin.
Open your mouths and speak with us. We are members of your own body, and we are formed from the same substance from which you are formed.
We are creatures of one God, and we are one soul. Do not be afraid. He does not cast you away. He does not reject you.
He does not turn away from you. I have learned from him that if you believe in him, you will feast at the table of his kingdom.”
Then those priests answered before the crowd, saying, “How can our mouth, which has led others astray, speak?
What have we to say? The faces of our hearts are blacker than our outward faces. We have no boldness to open our mouths and speak.
But this we know, believe, and affirm: he is the one God who created the world in his grace, and his beloved only Son is our Lord Jesus Christ.”
who took on a body from the holy virgin. Whether we die or live, we acknowledge no one else.
But woe to us if he does not have mercy on us and forgive us, because we have great wealth and perishable gold.
We acquired it from these souls. Now the governor wanted them to come near him, because they were far from the crowd
and were standing by themselves. But when people went to bring them forward and place them in the middle, the priests said,
“We beg you, do not soil your hands with our filth. We will not move forward from here
until the one in whose name we have believed wills it.” It was about the third hour of that day. The holy man spoke to the governor and said,
“My lord, order water to be brought into the baptismal font. We must baptize this crowd and speak the word of life to them.
And order banquets to be held throughout the city. As for anyone who lacks food, our Lord Jesus, who fed thousands in the wilderness,
will provide it for him.” Then the governor called his son Menelaus, who had come back to life, and said to him, “Take ten men with you,
and let each of them go and organize for you a hundred men from among those who have received the seal of baptism.
Let them arrange banquets and prepare a great feast.” They went and did as the governor had commanded. Meanwhile, Saint John
rose from the step on which he had been sitting, came to the priests, and took the hand of their leader, whose name was Apollo,
and the hand of the other, whose name was Dionysius. He brought them near him and spoke the word of God to them, explaining
and encouraging them. But Apollo and Dionysius, the priests, cried out,
“Have pity on us, Son of God, and bring us near your Father. We beg you: if we are held accountable for our wickedness,
let these people not be held accountable, because we led them astray from your way. We beg you, merciful Lord: have mercy, my Lord, on our wickedness.
If your justice judges us, let these people not be judged, for their wrongdoing is ours, my Lord.” And all the people were weeping.
When the baptismal font was ready, the governor gave orders, and oil was brought. Then Saint John stood up, prayed, and said,
“Glory to you, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.” They responded after him, “Amen.” And he said, “Lord God Almighty,
may your Holy Spirit come, rest, and dwell upon the oil and upon the water. May they bathe and be washed clean of impurity,
and receive the Holy Spirit through baptism. From now on may they call you ‘Our Father in heaven.’ Yes, my Lord, sanctify this water by your voice,
which cried out over the Jordan and pointed out our Lord Jesus with a finger: ‘This is my beloved Son, in whom I am pleased. Listen to him.’ You
are here, the very one who was over the Jordan. Yes, I beg you, my Lord, reveal yourself here before this crowd who have sincerely believed in you.
May the nations of the earth also hear that the city of Ephesus was the first to receive your good news, before all the other cities,
and became a twin sister to Edessa of the Parthians.” At that very moment, fire was blazing above the oil.
The angels spread their wings above the oil, and the whole assembly—men, women, and children—cried out:
“Holy, holy, holy is the mighty Lord, whose praises fill heaven and earth!” Immediately the vision was taken away.
The priests lay face down, weeping. Saint John approached and raised them up, and they said:
“We believe in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and we know nothing else.” John approached and washed the soot off them.
He anointed them with oil and baptized them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, for the remission of debts and the forgiveness of sins.
Saint John said to the governor, “Order them to go and bring fine dry bread and wine, while the whole crowd is being baptized.”
They went and arranged and prepared everything. When the whole crowd had been baptized, the priests said, “Our brothers, our fathers, and our children,
today we carry the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. Why do images of Satan’s daughter stand over the gates of our city?
Let us go, take them down, and burn them, and place the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ over every gate.” The whole crowd cried out:
“Where should we build a church?” Saint John was glad and rejoiced, and he said to the governor:
“See, my lord, what place pleases you.” They chose a beautiful place, carried the cross, and went there. They set up the cross there,
and crosses over the gates throughout the city. The saint prayed and offered the offering, and gave them communion in the body and blood of Christ.
They gathered there every Sunday, broke bread together, and shared in the body and blood of Christ.
They gathered there every Sunday, broke bread together, and shared in the body and blood of our Life-giver. After these things,
as the good news spread through the apostles, Nero, the unclean, defiled, and wicked emperor, heard everything that had happened in Ephesus.
He sent men to seize everything the governor possessed and imprisoned him. He also arrested Saint John and sent him into exile.
He threatened to destroy the city. After three days, believers from the city gathered
and consulted one another, saying, “Let us gather at the church and see what each person is willing to give, and collect a bribe
and offer it to this wicked ruler, so that he will give us back the man who turned us from error to our Lord.” When they had agreed on this,
they collected three hundred pounds of gold. They took ten men and boarded a ship to go to the wicked emperor Nero
and give him a bribe and bring the saint back. When they had traveled and entered Rome, at midnight, while the unclean Nero was sleeping,
the Lord sent an angel against him. He appeared to him blazing with fire and carrying a sword, and woke him. When Nero opened his eyes and looked at him,
he wailed and said, “I beg you, what have I to do with you?” The angel said to him, “Send back the man whom you took from Ephesus and sent into exile.
Otherwise, this sword will enter your unclean heart by sunrise.” The angel struck him and took away his speech.
He howled like a dog. When his servants heard his wailing, they came in and said to him, “What is wrong with you, my lord the emperor?”
He signaled, and they brought him ink and paper. He wrote: “Immediately, if possible today,
John son of Zebedee, the Galilean, whom you took from Ephesus, is to live there.” He also wrote and urgently sent word to Ephesus that everyone
who was imprisoned should be released and conduct himself as he wished. Sailors and armed men came and took the king’s signed orders.
They went down to the ship. They went and found John at midday, kneeling and praying.
They said to him, “The king has ordered us to take you back to where you were.” They took him and went down to the ship, and sailed peacefully across the sea.
They brought him as far as the gate of Ephesus and returned to Rome. Now those men who had brought the bribe,
when they heard that the holy man had returned to Ephesus, said this: “We worship you, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit,
because you have fulfilled the desire of those who fear you.” They boarded a ship, brought those three hundred pounds, and came. When they entered Ephesus,
they showed him the gold and related everything that had happened. There was joy throughout the city, and they consulted with one another.
They put the gold in a house and hired craftsmen. With it they built two churches for the worship of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The holy John went up and sat in the shelter. All the freeborn people of the region of Asia used to gather around him.
He taught and proclaimed the good news about our Lord Jesus. Nero’s decree remained in place, and he did not
dare to issue any further orders concerning the region of Asia. This wicked man was the one who killed Paul and Peter.
After a long time, when the apostles heard everything that had happened throughout the region of Ephesus, they were amazed and said,
“This matter is no great thing for our Lord Jesus, but it is astonishing to us.” Paul kept asking and inquiring about the apostles,
so that he might hear the story of the holy John. Every day and every hour he pleaded before God that he might be worthy to see him.
When the good news dawned in the world, it was the will of the Holy Spirit, and Matthew was moved to write a Gospel. After him came Mark,
and after him Luke. They wrote and sent word to the holy John that he too should write. They also informed him about Paul, who had joined the ranks of the apostles.
But the holy man did not wish to write, saying, “So that they would not say, ‘He is a boy,’ if Satan should sow confusion in the world.”
When the apostles had traveled through the lands, planted the cross, and taken hold of a cord in the four corners of creation, Simon Peter arose,
took Paul with him, and came to John in Ephesus. They rejoiced greatly and proclaimed our Lord Jesus without ceasing. They went up to
the holy man and found him praying. They greeted one another and rejoiced greatly. They related to one another everything that our Lord Jesus had done.
They appointed faithful men as priests. Peter and Paul entered Ephesus on Monday.
For five days they joyfully urged him to write a Gospel, but he was unwilling.
He said to them, “When it is the will of the Holy Spirit, I will write.” Now on Sunday night,
At the time when our Lord rose from the tomb, the apostles grew drowsy and fell asleep. At that very glorious time of the resurrection, the Holy Spirit descended.
The whole place where they were staying was ablaze. Those who were awake woke their companions.
They were amazed. John took a sheet of papyrus and wrote his Gospel in a single hour.
He gave it to Paul and Peter. When the sun rose, he went down to the house of prayer, and they read it before the whole city.
They prayed and shared in the body and blood of our Lord Jesus. They came to the holy man and stayed with him for thirty days.
Then they came to Jerusalem, to James, our Lord’s brother. From there they came to Antioch. The holy man lived in a shelter, summer and winter,
until he was a hundred and twenty years old. There his Lord buried him, in that very place, just as Moses was buried on Mount Nebo.
Everyone who believes and affirms the signs that our Lord performed through the apostles will receive mercy on the day of judgment.
For the Holy Spirit, who is in the Father and in the Son, everything is easy. As for the children of the church, without doubt,
let them offer praise without questioning, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.
Here ends the teaching of John son of Zebedee, who reclined on the breast of our Lord Jesus at supper, and who made disciples, taught, and baptized in the city of Ephesus.
